description: Curated visual composition recipes. These are positive visual priors, not fixed templates. Zones use normalized 0..1 coordinates and should be adapted to content.

references.why_it_works: One oversized statement creates immediate hierarchy; metadata becomes a quiet secondary layer instead of competing with the title.
references.adaptation_notes: Use the right-side visual only if it strengthens the concept; otherwise make typography occupy the full composition.

references.why_it_works: A decisive image crop creates visual richness without adding many small elements; text remains in one clean reading column.
references.adaptation_notes: Prefer one edge-to-edge crop over a floating stock photo.

references.why_it_works: One word or phrase owns the page while supporting explanation is intentionally subordinate.
references.adaptation_notes: Do not turn parallel bullets into numbered blocks; use this only when a genuine thesis can dominate.

references.why_it_works: A strong claim occupies one side; a narrow evidence rail gives proof, source and annotations without creating equal cards.
references.adaptation_notes: The evidence rail can be a figure, quote, case fact or compact chart.

references.why_it_works: Definition and example receive different visual weights, making the conceptual relationship clearer than two equal boxes.
references.adaptation_notes: The example should look like evidence/case material, not a decorative second card.

references.why_it_works: A single path makes causality and order explicit; steps are attached to one spine instead of floating as disconnected cards.
references.adaptation_notes: Use 3–6 meaningful steps and vary node weight if one stage matters more.

references.why_it_works: The system boundary is visually explicit and the main data/control path is highlighted, preventing a generic grid of modules.
references.adaptation_notes: Use the narrow right annotation column for design decisions, risks or constraints.

references.why_it_works: The takeaway number is read before the chart; the chart then proves rather than competes with the conclusion.
references.adaptation_notes: Highlight one series/number; suppress default chart chrome.

references.why_it_works: A large research figure owns the page while a caption/takeaway rail explains exactly what the audience should notice.
references.adaptation_notes: Use annotations/callouts sparingly; preserve figure legibility and source.

references.why_it_works: The recommended/preferred option gets larger visual weight; comparison is not forced into two equal columns when the conclusion is not equal.
references.adaptation_notes: Use equal columns only when the argument truly has equal weight.

references.why_it_works: Criteria form the reading spine and visual emphasis marks the decision, avoiding a feature-list card grid.
references.adaptation_notes: Use direct highlights/checks only for meaningful criteria; do not decorate every cell.

references.why_it_works: A large screenshot/figure is treated as evidence and only a few precise annotations explain what matters.
references.adaptation_notes: Crop aggressively enough that the audience can read the relevant UI/figure.

references.why_it_works: Milestones follow one visual path with varied emphasis, avoiding a row of identical date cards.
references.adaptation_notes: Vary milestone size only when importance differs.

references.why_it_works: Two dimensions turn a prose trade-off list into a spatial argument, making relationships immediately visible.
references.adaptation_notes: Axes must represent real decision dimensions, not arbitrary decorative labels.

references.why_it_works: The closing echoes the opening visual thesis and leaves one memorable statement instead of a generic 'Thank you' page.
references.adaptation_notes: Reuse one motif or phrase from the cover to create closure.

references.why_it_works: A strong typographic column system keeps dense citations readable without turning every source into a card.
references.adaptation_notes: Use hanging indents, numbering or author/year hierarchy rather than decorative boxes.

references.why_it_works: One image covering the full canvas plus a single text block reads as a designed cover rather than a template; a purposeful panel keeps the title legible instead of relying on a gradient.
references.adaptation_notes: Overlay text only on genuine negative space or an opaque panel; otherwise shift the crop so one exists.

references.why_it_works: A single unresolved question plus one striking fact creates immediate curiosity, which a table-of-contents card cannot.
references.adaptation_notes: Reserve for the first content page; do not stack several questions or turn it into an agenda list.

references.why_it_works: One image bleeding past the normal content frame dominates the page, so a single caption supplies meaning instead of many small decorative photos.
references.adaptation_notes: Decide the crop before writing the text; a small floating photo defeats this reference.

references.why_it_works: A short quote over a purposeful image makes one claim memorable while the image carries tone rather than information.
references.adaptation_notes: Keep quote text short and verify contrast against the real crop, not an assumed one.

references.why_it_works: A short definition anchors one column while a purpose-built diagram earns the other, so the concept is explained visually instead of restated in bullets.
references.adaptation_notes: The diagram must encode a real relationship, not repeat the sentence using shapes.

references.why_it_works: A left-to-right path of three to five steps shows order and hand-off, and unequal node weight marks the step that matters instead of four equal cards.
references.adaptation_notes: Use only when genuine order exists; otherwise switch to comparison or a main-cause structure.

references.why_it_works: A closed loop makes feedback and repetition legible; a linear row would misrepresent a process that never terminates.
references.adaptation_notes: Reserve the side rail for the exit condition or failure mode.

references.why_it_works: Layered bands express inclusion and scale, which a flat list or equal cards cannot, because band width becomes meaningful data.
references.adaptation_notes: Band width or height must encode a real quantity or scope, not decoration.

references.why_it_works: Two states share one axis so the change itself becomes the message, and a shared divider makes the delta readable at a glance.
references.adaptation_notes: Use identical framing and crop for both states or the comparison becomes misleading.

references.why_it_works: A quiet editorial table with one emphasized column beats a card grid when many values must be compared across the same dimensions.
references.adaptation_notes: Remove vertical rules and zebra shading unless they carry meaning; emphasize one column or row.

references.why_it_works: One dominant primary metric plus a supporting strip reads as a decision summary rather than a row of four equal stat tiles.
references.adaptation_notes: Give one metric real dominance; identical stat tiles are the failure mode.

references.why_it_works: Repeated charts on one shared scale reveal a pattern across groups that a single stacked chart would hide.
references.adaptation_notes: Share axes across panels and label once; per-panel legends add noise.

references.why_it_works: One oversized quotation with clear attribution gives a single voice full authority while surrounding commentary stays subordinate.
references.adaptation_notes: Use a real, attributable quotation; never fabricate a source, speaker or study.

references.why_it_works: A recap that traces the deck's own argument path reinforces retention, unlike a neutral bullet summary detached from the narrative.
references.adaptation_notes: Numbering must mirror the actual argument sequence, not restate parallel bullets.

references.why_it_works: An oversized section numeral plus one line of orientation gives the audience a clear breath between chapters without a decorative card.
references.adaptation_notes: Keep dividers sparse; more than three in a short deck breaks rhythm.

references.why_it_works: Ending on an explicit next step or ask makes the deck actionable and prevents a hollow thank-you slide.
references.adaptation_notes: Use when the scenario expects a proposal or decision; otherwise prefer closing-callback.
